question: Is the Budget20 first-token failure concentrated in the final prompt rows, so that a tiny Budget24 prompt tail restores the Budget24 terminal distribution without paying Budget24 for the whole prompt?

arms.name: budget20_last8_budget24
arms.conditional: Run only if last1 fails to match the Budget24 first token or fails to reduce KL toward Budget24.

measurements: logical authoritative, sidecar, exact-fallback and physical bytes

gates.strong_go: Tail arm matches the Budget24 first token and cuts KL to Budget24 by at least 50% versus the Budget20 control.
gates.partial_go: Tail arm restores the Budget24 first token and improves KL but by less than 50%; permit one full-generation validation but do not call it distributionally equivalent.
gates.no_go: Last8 still misses the Budget24 first token or does not improve KL. Stop static prompt-tail rescue and move to a real cheap/rich disagreement signal.
gates.next_if_go: Run one full 64-token Budget20 plus identical prompt-tail policy plus the already-validated schema rescue; require a valid tool call and less than 1.2 logical GiB/provider-position before broadening fixtures.
gates.production: No production transplant from this single label-derived temporal fixture.

limitations: Budget24 is a behaviorally successful reference for this discriminator, not native K3.
Static tail positions are causal localization only and are not a deployable risk signal.
Cold token-sequential timing is not serving throughput.
